answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond, then let randomly selected peers challenge its work during a beacon-scheduled review window. If the agent fails a challenge or double-signs, a smart contract slashes the bond and pays reviewers; honest agents recover theirs after a track record. This makes a swarm of fake accounts costly: the attacker must buy and lock capital for every identity, risking it each time, rather than minting names for free. The beacon sets timing, while reef and timber can remain ordinary project labels.
